newsitem.title: USA: Seabrokers says it has hired away several brokers.
newsitem.headline: Seabrokers says it has hired away several brokers.

text.p: U.S. shipbrokering group Seabrokers Inc, a wholly-owned subsidiary of H Clarkson & Co of the U.K, said Tuesday it has hired away five leading brokers from industry rival Atlantic Chartering.
Five of the eight brokers currently employed by Atlantic will join Seabrokers as of January 1, a move which effectively puts Atlantic out of business.

"We're taking five brokers from Atlantic and they are coming into our offices," Seabrokers president Richard Bryn told Reuters. But he stressed that the hirings do not represent merger of the two companies' assets.
The staff additions bring the total number of brokers employed by Stamford, Connecticut-based Seabrokers, to 14.
Shipping industry sources said the move by Seabrokers seeks to to broaden its focus to include tanker fixtures in the Middle and Far East.
"Seabrokers has been looking to add manpower that has knowledge in other directions," said one industry broker, who requested anonymity.

The addition of Atlantic head broker Larry Cirillo, who will become vice president of Seabrokers, should help the company to expand its scope beyond its current emphasis in the Western Hemisphere, he added.
"The bigger shops have dominated the markets where the small shops were once strong, so it makes sense for them to merge," said another industry broker.
Atlantic Chartering is likely to cease operations in the next few months, sources said, but it was unclear whether the three brokers who are not heading to Seabrokers will form their own company.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
